clue.text: Disadvantage for young person in a race?

definitions.text: Disadvantage for young person in a race?

blocks.note: surface reading: a small child hampered in some contest
setter's reading: a horse race for two-year-olds, where weights are allotted to even the field

explanation.surface: A toddler struggles to keep up in a running race.
explanation.walkthrough: A NURSERY HANDICAP is a British horse race for two-year-olds; 'young person' is really a young horse, and the handicap is the race itself, not a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing jargon names juvenile weighted contests after the nursery, so the question-marked phrase describes one fairly.

clue.text: Tobacco tin decorated with a flower

blocks.note: a can is a tin container
the aster is a daisy-like garden plant

explanation.surface: A tobacco tin painted with a floral design.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaster is a coarse dark pipe tobacco, named from the rush baskets it was once shipped in.

clue.text: Joint headdress

blocks.note: first meaning: a corner joint where two bevelled pieces of wood meet
second meaning: the tall pointed hat worn by a bishop

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a shared hat; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpenters cut a bevelled corner joint, and bishops wear a tall ceremonial cap; one word names both.

clue.text: Carrying out orders to debit one, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the preceding letters are only one possible arrangement, so they may be reordered

blocks.note: the two words supply all eight letters

explanation.surface: A bank clerk dutifully follows instructions to charge one account.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone compliant and dutiful does what they are told, following commands without resistance.

clue.text: Thus odd pet is held to be infected

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of the ordinary, so the following word's letters are rearranged
something held is gripped inside another, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to flag a quotation as exact
the three letters shuffled

explanation.surface: A strange pet is thought to carry an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound that has gone septic is contaminated by bacteria, the condition of being infected.

clue.text: What doctor ordered for the management

blocks.note: first meaning: medical care prescribed for a patient
second meaning: the way something or someone is handled or dealt with

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes a course for the company bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A physician prescribes a course of care, and the way people are handled or dealt with is likewise how they are treated.

clue.text: Decoration in small capitals at top of list

blocks.note: sc. is the printer's abbreviation for small capitals
a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: A heading set in small capitals adorns the top of a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At top of' places the first piece above the second in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scroll is a spiral ornament carved in architecture or furniture, a form of decoration.

clue.text: Perpetual peace unwelcome to a compiler, perhaps

definitions.text: Perpetual peace unwelcome to a compiler, perhaps

blocks.note: surface reading: an unbroken harmony between people, with no angry exchange ever
setter's reading: a world without any puzzle for a setter to compile would end the job

explanation.surface: Lasting harmony that would put a puzzle setter out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a relationship without quarrels, read literally, means no puzzle at all, which a crossword compiler would hate.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes constant harmony, and literally means the absence of the very puzzle a setter produces.

clue.text: Girl on the road can be unfriendly

blocks.note: Una is a girl's name
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written with I for 1
if you can do something you are able

explanation.surface: A young woman driving can turn surly.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords treat the digit as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking amiability means being disagreeable and cold, the opposite of friendly.

clue.text: Regret swathing church in frilly cloth

indicators.note: to swathe is to wrap something up, so the first word wraps around the next

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone regrets draping a church in fussy frilled fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a pleated or gathered strip of fabric used as a frill trimming garments.

clue.text: Disputed mineral colour

blocks.note: spar is a crystalline mineral such as feldspar
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Geologists argue over the colour of a mineral sample.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue or exchange blows, so having sparred means having disputed.

clue.text: Got up after meal to get a flower

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the next one, so the clue's order is swapped in the answer

blocks.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal
past tense of rise

explanation.surface: Someone stands up after tea to go and pick a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the first-named piece behind the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea rose is a hybrid garden variety whose scent is said to resemble tea.

clue.text: Liturgy that sounds in order

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by how a word is pronounced rather than spelt

blocks.note: something in order is all right, correct

explanation.surface: A church service that seems perfectly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a prescribed religious ceremony, the set form of words in a liturgy.

clue.text: Dessert for attractive girl singer

blocks.note: a peach is old slang for a lovely young woman
Dame Nellie Melba was the Australian opera soprano

explanation.surface: A pudding served to a pretty young singer.
explanation.definitionFit: This classic sweet of peaches, ice cream and raspberry sauce was created by Escoffier and named for the soprano.

clue.text: They write stories about drinks

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Journalists famously filing copy about a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists who gather and file news items write stories for papers and broadcasters.

clue.text: Most difficult animal carrying little boy

indicators.note: carrying means bearing something within, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: a hart is a male deer
Des is short for Desmond, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A beast of burden struggles with a small child on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of hard, meaning the toughest or least easy of all.

clue.text: He gives warning to senior pupil

blocks.note: first meaning: one who watches and admonishes
second meaning: an older schoolchild given duties over younger ones

explanation.surface: A teacher cautions an older student.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin monere means to warn, and in British schools a prefect-like older child entrusted with duties shares the name.

clue.text: Regulate the cost of fashion?

blocks.note: a mode is a fashion or style
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Controlling what clothes cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cost of fashion' puts the charge after the style, so the pieces read in reverse of the clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate is to keep within limits or control, as a referee or chair regulates.

clue.text: Timothy's one song sung with bashfulness

indicators.note: sung means voiced out loud, so the word is taken by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: Tim is short for Timothy
Roman numeral one
a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: Timothy shyly performs his one little song.
explanation.walkthrough: The joined pieces, said out loud, match the answer's pronunciation; only the spelling of the final syllables differs.
explanation.definitionFit: Timidity is shyness and lack of confidence, the same quality as bashfulness.

clue.text: Sailor to keep going round with vocalist

blocks.note: Admiral Lord Nelson, Britain's most famous sailor
to eddy is to swirl in circles

explanation.surface: A seaman keeps circling with a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Eddy was an American baritone famous for 1930s film musicals with Jeanette MacDonald.

clue.text: Friend turning to follow pet

indicators.note: turning round makes a word face the other way, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
to dog is to follow closely

explanation.surface: A friend turns round to follow a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pampered dog kept as a companion; figuratively a fawning follower.

clue.text: Final flower made to last

blocks.note: the end is the final part
a flower is something that flows, a river: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A last bloom was preserved to stay fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword trick for a river; the Ure runs through North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to persist or continue over time, which is what lasting means.

clue.text: I'm having second thoughts on children ...

blocks.note: taken as written
a PS, postscript, adds afterthoughts to a letter

explanation.surface: A parent reconsiders the matter of having kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 24 across, which refers back to these mischievous children.
explanation.definitionFit: Imps are mischievous little ones, a playful word for naughty kids.

clue.text: Leaps round part of flower

indicators.note: round suggests turning about, so the letters are moved into a new arrangement

blocks.note: five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone jumps around a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like outer segments of a blossom, forming the calyx around the petals.

clue.text: ... one of whom spoiled duet as charged

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so the word that follows is broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: whom refers back to the children of 22 across, so one of them is a single little rascal
four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: One naughty child wrecked a duet and was accused of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute is to attribute a fault or crime to someone, so imputed means laid to their charge.

clue.text: Wonder about first engagement, if forced to make a second bequest

indicators.note: first tells us to keep only the opening letter of the word that follows
about means placed around, so one word surrounds the other
forced suggests something wrenched out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone muses whether a broken first engagement means changing their will.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to bestow money or property; doing so again is giving a further gift or legacy.

clue.text: Love to have a morning to see round old city

blocks.note: taken as written
m is short for morning, as in a.m.
O is round in shape
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A romantic morning's sightseeing tour of an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See round' looks like a sightseeing phrase, but 'round' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is the French loanword for a love affair or romantic passion.

clue.text: One holding back a muscle

blocks.note: first meaning: a surgical instrument that keeps tissue drawn aside
second meaning: a muscle that draws a body part inward

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone restraining a strongman; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons use a clamp-like instrument to keep wound edges apart, and anatomy names muscles that pull parts back the same way.
